Christopher Hollyday

Christopher Hollyday is an American alto saxophonist associated with jazz. Christopher Hollyday was born in Bridgeport, Connecticut, on February 3, 1970. He returned with the album "Telepathy" in 2018 and released "Dialogue" two years later. In 1988 he led a band at the Village Vanguard. Hollyday moved to San Diego in 1996 and later became band director at Valley Center High School. He released "Treaty" on his own Jazzbeat label in 1985 and followed it with "Oh, Brother!" the next year. Charlie Parker was a strong influence on his playing. He began playing the saxophone when he was nine years old. His playing attracted praise for its technical facility, although some critics found it lacking in expression. His career has included performing, recording, composing, and teaching.

He grew up in a musical family, and his father listened extensively to bebop. After four albums for RCA/Novus, he was dropped from the label while developing his own musical voice. His playing attracted praise for its technical facility, although some critics found it lacking in expression. He began playing the saxophone when he was nine years old. Charlie Parker was a strong influence on his playing. He returned with the album "Telepathy" in 2018 and released "Dialogue" two years later. Around 2013 he shifted more of his work toward private teaching, giving him additional time to perform. His later career combined jazz performance with music education.
